title: docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md never says how to choose a profile's max_tokens, which is the one non-obvious decision in authoring one
description:
Found while working LCLI-640 (2026-09-29). Filed rather than absorbed: the deliverable is a docs change, LCLI-640's is a profile.

The runbook is 126 lines and is the authoritative how-to for authoring and operating a profile. It documents the file format, discovery, validation, compilation, saved artifacts and rollback -- and says nothing about how to choose max_tokens. The field appears once, as the unexplained number 4000 in the step-1 example. Step 1's prose covers naming and references and stops there.

This is not a stylistic gap. Sizing is the only decision in a profile that has no obvious answer, and two separate efforts have now had to derive it by experiment rather than read it: OPAG-33 swept 10k-24k to set implementation 20000 / review 18000 / verification 16000, and LCLI-640 swept 8k-24k across four tasks to set documentation 20000. Whichever author comes next repeats that work from scratch, because the result lives in the .toml files rather than in the runbook.

The derivation is also NOT the obvious one, which is what makes writing it down worth more than the cost of the section. LCLI-640's thirteen-budget sweep measured that the omission curve is not monotone in max_tokens: on one task, 20000 selected 23 of 80 ranked blocks while 20500 selected 5, because context ranks COMPLETE blocks and a larger budget can admit one large high-scoring block whole, displacing several smaller ones. So the intuitive rule -- raise the budget until nothing more is dropped -- is wrong and can make a pack strictly worse. The working test OPAG-33 used (and LCLI-640 reused) is that no source scoring 9 or above may be fully omitted, read off the allowed-source catalog, with the sweep read as a table rather than as a curve that converges. LCLI-642 is the checking half of this -- it gates a profile whose declared sources cannot fit at all -- and is complementary, not a substitute: "it fits" and "the budget was chosen well" are different questions.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow: add a short section to docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md on choosing max_tokens, carrying the sweep method, the >=9 test, the non-monotonicity warning and a pointer to the measurement. It should NOT restate LCLI-640's or OPAG-33's numbers as universal -- they are per-bundle measurements -- and it should NOT propose a change to lore's assembler, which would be a design question for the orchestrator.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md explains how to choose a profile max_tokens, including the sweep method and the >=9 omission test, in the runbook section that already owns profile authoring
The section states that the omission curve is not monotone in the budget and that a larger budget can yield a strictly worse pack, so raising it until nothing more is dropped is not the rule
The section does not present any other bundle's budget as universal, and proposes no change to the pack assembler
bun run lore check and bun test exit 0 (test/ pins operational-doc text)
